blocks.text: Matter exists in four states: solid, liquid, gas and plasma. The simplest form of matter is the gaseous state, and most of the matter around us is solid. Liquids are less common than solids, gases and plasmas, because the liquid state of any substance exists only within a relatively narrow range of temperature and pressure. The kinetic molecular theory of gases helps to understand the properties of gases, liquids and solids.

items: Gases have no definite shape or volume; the volume of a gas is the volume of its container.
Ideal gases have zero particle volume.

The molecules of a gas are widely separated and most of the volume of a gas is empty space (nearly 99.9 per cent), which is why gases are compressed easily. When a gas expands suddenly, cooling takes place: the Joule-Thomson effect.
The pressure of a gas is due to the collisions of its molecules with the walls of the container.
There are negligible intermolecular forces in ideal gases.
